I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, so I can’t tell you your exact download/upload speeds. But you can check it yourself in a few quick ways: | Method | How to do it | |--------|--------------| | **Web browser** | Visit (or ) and click “Go” – it will automatically ping the nearest server and report download, upload, and ping. | | **Command‑line (Windows)** | If you have PowerShell, you can run the built‑in `Test-NetConnection` cmdlet:
`Test-NetConnection -ComputerName www.speedtest.net -Port 80` – this gives you latency and a basic connectivity test. | | **Command‑line (Linux/macOS)** | Install the `speedtest-cli` tool and run:
`speedtest-cli --simple` – it will output download, upload, and ping. | | **Mobile app** | Download the official Speedtest app from Google Play or the App Store; it’s free and gives you a quick readout. | If you want a quick one‑liner on Windows that uses PowerShell’s `Invoke-WebRequest` to hit a public speed‑test endpoint, you could try something like: ```powershell $uri = "https://api.speedtest.net/speedtest-servers-static.php" Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $uri -Method Get ``` (That just pulls the server list; for a full test you’d need the dedicated client.) So the easiest route is to open a browser and go to Speedtest.net or Fast.com. That will give you a reliable measurement of your current internet speed.
